{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   -p qcpu_exp
#   -A DD-23-135
#   -n 1
#   --comment "use:vtune=2022.2.0"
#   -t 0:10:00
#   --mail-type END
#   -J AVS-vtune

#flux: --job-name=AVS-vtune
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: --time-limit=10m

# Omitted Slurm option: -p qcpu_exp (partition)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different priority/limits or on different hardware (or be rejected by policy).

# Omitted Slurm option: -A DD-23-135 (account)
# Flux accounting/project selection is site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may be charged to a default account or be rejected by policy.

# Omitted Slurm option: --comment "use:vtune=2022.2.0"
# Flux does not have a universally portable equivalent for Slurm comments.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but tooling that relies on the comment may not function.

# Omitted Slurm option: --mail-type END
# Flux does not provide a universal, built-in email notification directive in batch scripts.
# Performance implication: none on runtime performance, but you will not receive automatic completion emails.

# Slurm variable $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR is not set under Flux.
cd "${FLUX_JOB_SUBMIT_DIR:-$PWD}"

ml intel-compilers/2022.1.0 CMake/3.23.1-GCCcore-11.3.0 VTune/2022.2.0-intel-2021b

[ -d build_vtune ] && rm -rf build_vtune
mkdir -p build_vtune
cd build_vtune

CC=icc CXX=icpc cmake ..
make

for threads in 18 36; do
    for builder in "ref" "loop" "tree"; do
        rm -rf vtune-${builder}-${threads}
        vtune -collect threading -r vtune-${builder}-${threads} -app-working-dir . -- \
          ./PMC --builder ${builder} -t ${threads} --grid 128 ../data/bun_zipper_res3.pts
    done
done
"
}
